items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-06-06
items.q: every summer from then on until I was about 18, my father would let me go down to Houston and play with Sid Iles.

ctx.x: Well Paul, you talk about enthusiasm. We would ride 250 and 300 miles in the old raggedy bus on the highway and get to town, wash up and get a little breakfast and go to rehearsal. Some guy would be writing arrangements all the way to the next town and then have to go to work that night and travel the next night. Is that enthusiasm? Sure has. My real name is Lawrence Douglas. I'm L.D. Harris. My real name is Lawrence Douglas. I'm L.D. Harris.

I'm born and raised in Brenham, Texas. That's about 165 miles from here. It's on H and TC between Austin and Houston, Texas. And I started out playing music between the ages of 13 and 14, started studying music. They organized a boys band there. I had a fellow who had been in the service by the name of Gus Allen. He was a boy band. He was a boy band. He was a boy band. Something to keep us off the street I guess, keep us off the devil. So they did. And I was a boy band. I was a boy band. I was a boy band. I was a…
Want to go there? One time? Yeah.
